title: The Upshot’s New Deputy Editor for Visuals and Data
body_markdown:
Nadja Popovich, an exceptional journalist and colleague, joins The Upshot as deputy editor for visuals and data. Read more from editor of The Upshot, Jonathan Ellis.


I’m thrilled to announce that Nadja Popovich, an exceptional journalist and colleague, is returning to The Times as The Upshot’s deputy editor for visuals and data.


It’s no exaggeration to say that everyone who has worked with Nadja is excited that she’s coming back: She brings curiosity, insight, rigor and creativity to all her work and is a joy to work with. Now, she’ll help supercharge The Upshot’s innovative approach to explaining the news and the world around us.


Most recently, Nadja was a senior editor on the Bloomberg News data team, where she edited collaborative projects on a range of topics, including a memorable look at


[New York City’s wealthy renters who are struggling](https://www.bloomberg.com/graphics/2025-nyc-wealthy-renters-housing-crisis/) amid the housing crisis and an investigation into the booming business of


[“zombie” second mortgages](https://www.bloomberg.com/graphics/2025-zombie-debt-collectors-mortgage-loans/) . She also continued to report on


[energy](https://www.bloomberg.com/graphics/2026-electricity-price-utility-gap/) , a long-term focus, most recently exploring America’s growing


[power bill divide](https://www.bloomberg.com/graphics/2026-electricity-price-utility-gap/) .


And she helped edit and produce a graphic novel that took readers inside one woman’s


[“digital arrest,”](https://www.bloomberg.com/graphics/2025-india-digital-arrest-by-phone-graphic-novel/) part of a scam wave sweeping India. The project won the 2026


[Pulitzer Prize](https://www.pulitzer.org/winners/anand-rk-and-suparna-sharma-contributors-and-natalie-obiko-pearson-bloomberg) for Illustrated Reporting and Commentary


.


Prior to Bloomberg, Nadja was a graphics reporter and editor on The Times’s Climate desk for seven years. Among her work from that era,


[“How Much Hotter Is Your Hometown Than When You Were Born?”](https://www.nytimes.com/interactive/2018/08/30/climate/how-much-hotter-is-your-hometown.html) is still a classic (and very Upshottian). Other standout projects included a graphics-driven series on


[efforts](https://www.nytimes.com/interactive/2023/04/14/climate/electric-car-heater-everything.html)[to remake](https://www.nytimes.com/interactive/2024/05/07/climate/battery-electricity-solar-california-texas.html)[the U.S. energy system](https://www.nytimes.com/interactive/2023/06/12/climate/us-electric-grid-energy-transition.html) and a 3-D reconstruction of how a massive Western wildfire


[fueled its own extreme weather](https://www.nytimes.com/interactive/2021/10/19/climate/dixie-fire-storm-clouds-weather.html?smid=nytcore-ios-share) .


Hannah Fairfield, senior editor for enterprise, said Nadja was a linchpin in establishing Climate as a visual-first team nearly a decade ago.


“Her vision and creativity are an incredible match for The Upshot,” Hannah said. “I’m excited to see where she will take it.”


We are, too. Nadja starts today. Please join me in welcoming her back.


— Jonathan
